prompt: Implement rotateRight so it returns a NEW array containing the elements of a rotated right by k positions, without modifying the original array. k may be larger than the array length.
explanation: Rotating right by k moves the element at index i to index (i + k) % length, so the modulo operator handles both the wrap-around and any k larger than the array length. Building the result in a brand-new array is what keeps the original untouched. An empty array needs a guard because k % 0 would throw an ArithmeticException.
hints: Reduce k first: rotating by the array length returns the same order, so only k % a.length matters.
Create a new array of the same length and copy each element to its shifted position instead of moving things inside a.
Element a[i] lands at index (i + k % n) % n in the result. Watch out for the empty array before doing any % n.
